question: Kona coffee in Hawaii grows below 1,000 m, yet rivals high-mountain coffees. What does altitude mostly stand in for?
answer: Cooler temperatures that slow ripening. Arabica does best at mean temperatures of about 18 to 21 °C, and slow ripening lets beans build more sugars and acids. Near the equator that climate begins around 1,200 to 2,000 m. Kona, at about 19° north, finds it far lower: height was standing in for temperature.
move: Before crediting a factor, ask what else changes along with it.
ask: When I credit one factor for a result, what else changed along with it?
trap: Crediting the height itself, as if thin air made the flavour.
source: DaMatta & Ramalho, Braz. J. Plant Physiol., 2006
reference: DaMatta & Ramalho, Impacts of drought and temperature stress on coffee physiology and production: a review, Brazilian Journal of Plant Physiology, 2006
